title: Arzawa lands of western Anatolia
summary: Arzawa was the Hittites' name for a kingdom and wider group of Late Bronze Age states in western Anatolia, including Mira, Hapalla and the Seha River Land. Mursili II of Hatti defeated its king Uhha-Ziti in his third regnal year. Where the lands lay, and whether the capital Apasa was at Ephesus, is still disputed.

uncertainty.note: Arzawa is attested in Hittite records; its fullest description is the 14th-century BCE Annals of Mursili II. Earlier and later bounds were not confirmed on an opened scholarly page.

as_recorded.value: the fourteenth century B. C (political organization described in Mursil's Annals)

where.modern_name: Ayasuluk Hill near Selçuk (Ephesus), Türkiye, one proposed site of Apasa; the lands spanned western Anatolia
where.historical_name: Arzawa, with its capital Apasa; later Hittite vassal states Mira, Hapalla and Seha River Land

importance.justification: Arzawa was the main Hittite rival in the west and is central to debates on Anatolia's links with the Aegean.

reviewer_note: Coordinator review: removed a Wikipedia-mirror source (HandWiki) and narrowed the span to the 14th century BCE that Garstang supports. Least sure of location: Garstang placed Apasa near Antiphellus (Kaş), a modern view puts it at Ephesus, and the Seha River Land is also debated; the 1700–1300 BCE span is a loose reference figure.
